AcJson.description: AC sweep in JSON: validity first, then the bode rows only when valid.

coverage.description: Honest "N of M" coverage annotation, distinct from `validity`. Non-gating.

nets.description: Per-net bode rows, present only when valid AND the net has a signal path.

no_signal_path_nets.description:
Nets that were requested but had no signal path (all points at the floor)
and so were omitted from `nets`. Empty when the whole sweep is invalid
(the `valid:false` + `reason` carries that case). Listed so a partially
valid sweep never silently drops a net.

not_found_nets.description:
Requested `--ac-node` names that don't exist in the circuit at all (their
bode is empty, distinct from "exists but no signal path"). Surfaced so the
JSON matches the text path's "net not found" warning instead of silently
dropping the net.

reason.description: Set only when `valid` is false: the named reason, listing offending refs.

ArtifactId.description:
Stable index into one validated run inventory. The inner index is private;
only [`EvidenceRegistry::add_artifact`] can mint one.

ArtifactKind.description: The normalized input format. Shared by provenance producers and renderers.

ArtifactProvenance.description: One input artifact: what it was, what it gave the run, what in it was ignored, and which cross-checks it passed.

assumptions.description:
Assumptions this artifact's limitations raised, by id, so the inventory
row and the assumption registry cross-reference instead of duplicating
text.

ignored.description: What in it was deliberately not used.

kind.description:
What the normalizer recognised it as: "kicad_pcb", "altium_pcbdoc",
"gerber_archive", "odbpp", "ipc2581", "board_code", "elf", "hex",
"toml", and so on.

path.description:
Path as the user gave it, not canonicalized: the report must read back
in the user's own vocabulary.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the bytes read (of the archive, for archives). Empty only
for a gerber DIRECTORY, where there is no single file to hash.

ArtifactRole.description: What role an input artifact played in the run.

oneOf.description: A board layout.
A schematic.
A netlist.
A fabrication archive (gerbers, ODB++, IPC-2581).
A firmware image.
A bill of materials.
A CI spec / assertion file.
A waiver file.
A model pack or models directory.
An MCU / SoC descriptor.

Assumption.description: One thing the run took as true, or deliberately did not examine, without evidence for it, with the four sentences that say what, why, what it costs, and what would close it.

because.description: Why the run had to assume it, one sentence.

consequence.description: What it does to results, one sentence.

expires.description:
Waived assumptions only: the `YYYY-MM-DD` the waiver lapses. `None` for
every run-derived kind, since an expiry on a machine observation would
mean nothing.

kind.description: What kind of gap this is. Drives [`EvidenceStatus`].

replacement.description:
The replacement path: what a user does so this stops being an
assumption. Always actionable, never "n/a".

statement.description: What is being taken as true, one sentence, present tense.

AssumptionId.description:
Stable identity for one assumption within a run. Deterministic:
`"{kind_slug}:{subject}"`, e.g. `"open-part:R7"`,
`"not-exercised:i2c0/U4"`, `"not-checked:drc"`,
`"waived:si/controlled_impedance/DDR_CLK"`. Re-running the same board yields
the same ids, so an acknowledgment file can name one, a diff can track one
across runs, and a renderer can cross-reference one.

The subject keeps its own case (a reference designator is `R7`, not `r7`)
and reserved bytes are percent-encoded, so distinct subjects never collapse
while the kind slug remains everything before the first `:`.

AssumptionKind.description:
What kind of gap an [`Assumption`] records. The kind, not the wording, is
what [`EvidenceMap::derive_status`] reads, so adding a variant is a policy
decision about what undermines a conclusion.

oneOf.description: An unresolved part defaulted to an open circuit.

A model stood in for the real part: an engine fallback entry, or a
substitute MCU core.

A pin's role was inferred from the pin-rule table, not read from the
schematic.

A parameter took a documented default because the source carried no
value.

Every placed part was treated as fitted because the input carries no
BOM or populate flag.

A whole check could not run on this input class and reported
"not checked" instead of a vacuous green.

The run happened but never exercised this element: a bus device never
addressed, an ADC channel whose injections the backend dropped,
firmware that never executed.

The result was produced at reduced fidelity by a documented degraded
mechanism: heuristic bus framing, a strapless MCU model, a net held by
an ideal source.

The producing parser has a known limitation that can fabricate or miss
findings here.

A human overrode a finding, with a reason and an expiry. The gating
machinery stays in the waiver code; this is the surfaced record.

AssumptionSource.description:
Which stage of the run raised the assumption. Mirrors the pipeline, so a
reader can tell an input-format limitation from a binder guess from a co-sim
coverage gap.

oneOf.description: An input reader (extract).
The binder, turning connectivity plus models into a circuit.
The co-sim scheduler.
The analog solver.
A check (DRC, SI, lint, ampacity, coverage).
A human, through a waiver or an override.

BindSummary.description:
The bind report, summarised by role rather than a single flat percentage.

"How many parts resolved" is the wrong unit when the 17% that did not are the
entire active circuit. The honest metrics are: did the MCU and the active
power ICs bind, and which active-path parts are open?

active_path_unresolved.description: Unresolved parts on connected nets (the active path), each annotated.

critical_parts_bound.description:
`"M/N"`, active ICs (MCU + U/IC-prefixed parts) that bound, over the
total active ICs on the board. The metric, not a bare percentage.

mcu_bound.description: True when at least one MCU bound.

resolved_but_open_active.description:
RESOLVED parts (incl. MCUs bound as `BindOutcome::Mcu`) that nonetheless
carry an open-pin warning while sitting on a live circuit. These are not
in `active_path_unresolved` (their outcome is not `Unresolved`), but an
active IC here still fails to drive its nets, so it must be surfaced as a
coverage caveat. Never empty implies untrustworthy thermal/AC results.

BootGateJson.description:
One row of the boot-state panel: a transistor gate and what the firmware does
to it at power-up (`driven_high` / `driven_low` / `floating`). Informational
(reported, not judged), so a consumer can read it without it being a verdict.

CheckCoverage.description:
Coverage is distinct from [`Validity`]. `Validity` stays BINARY and drives
exit 3. `CheckCoverage` is the honest "N of M active parts actually entered
this check" metric: it is ALWAYS emittable and NEVER changes the exit code on
its own (the partial-coverage thermal escalation is opt-in behind
`--strict-thermal`). `partial == true` means a renderer should print a
coverage caveat even though the check itself produced rows.

dissipating_count.description: Devices that actually produced a row in the check's table.

open_active_on_live_circuit.description: Active ICs left open on the live circuit (unresolved + resolved-but-open).

partial.description:
True => the renderer should surface a coverage caveat. Set when at least
one row exists but an active IC on the live circuit is open/unresolved.

resolved_fraction.description:
Covered active ICs / total active ICs, clamped to `[0, 1]`: how much of the
active circuit the check actually modelled. `1.0` when every active IC is
covered (or there are none, vacuously complete); low when power ICs are
open/unresolved.

total_active_count.description: Active ICs on the live circuit that the check should have covered.

Contribution.description: One concrete thing an artifact contributed to the run.

detail.description:
The specifics, one sentence, e.g. "netlist read from the document's
LogicalNet section, not reverse-engineered from copper".

parts.description: Nearby part names on the net (best-effort, may be empty).
`"REF.role"` of every enabled modelled push-pull output on the net.

t_s.description: Sim time (s) at which both sides were first seen driving together.

CosimFailedWindow.description:
One sim-time window `[start_s, end_s)` where the analog solve failed to
converge and the co-sim held stale voltages. Reported so a consumer knows the
exact span that cannot be trusted rather than inferring a quiet run.

reason.description:
The solver's own refusal message for this window: the blame clause
naming the net that refused to settle, the devices on it, and any
near-zero-ohm link poisoning the matrix (E29). Defaulted (and omitted
from JSON) when empty, so an older consumer keeps parsing.

CosimFallbackWindow.description:
One sim-time window `[start_s, end_s)` whose answer was produced by a
per-chunk fallback integration rung after the primary analog solve failed
there. `method` is the rung's stable name
(`crate::scheduler::ChunkFallbackMethod::as_str`), `accuracy` its stated
cost, so the record travels with the number it qualifies. Minimal on
purpose: shaped so a typed error-budget/provenance spine can absorb it
later as one provenance tag per window.

CosimJson.description:
Machine-readable co-sim summary (today only emitted as CLI text). Populated
from the headless run + the MCU binding. `substituted` is true when the part
the user asked for was modelled by a less-specific core (Track B).

activity_summary.description: Top-N nets by activity: name, toggle count, observed min/max voltage.

adc_dropped.description:
ADC channels whose per-chunk injections the MCU backend DROPPED because
the platform carries no injection map (U3 finding 1). Non-empty means
the analog solve drove these nets but the firmware NEVER received a
sample, analog readings on those pins are meaningless, and this run
cannot vouch for them. Empty (and omitted) on full coverage.

analog_valid.description:
False once any chunk's analog solve failed to converge: the run held stale
node voltages over `failed_windows` and cannot vouch for analog-derived
findings there (05 §3b, refuse rather than fake). A fully valid run reports
`true` with an empty `failed_windows`, so the common shape is unchanged and
existing consumers keep parsing.

backend.description: The actual backend string from `BindOutcome::Mcu { backend }`.

driver_contention.description:
Runtime driver contention: nets where the firmware configured an MCU
pin as a push-pull OUTPUT while an enabled modelled push-pull output
was already driving (the model-vs-MCU case the static output-contention
lint documents as out of its reach). Waveforms touching these nets are
untrustworthy from `t_s` on. One entry per offending net. Empty (and
omitted) on a healthy run.

failed_windows.description:
Sim-time windows `[start_s, end_s)` where the analog solve failed. Empty
(and omitted from JSON) on a valid run.

fallback_windows.description:
Sim-time windows solved by a per-chunk FALLBACK integration rung after
the primary solve failed there, each carrying the method that produced
it and that method's accuracy cost. These windows are solved (they do
not make the run analog-invalid) but their numbers are second-class:
a consumer reading a waveform is entitled to know which spans came from
a more dissipative method. Empty (and omitted) when the primary path
carried the whole run.

realtime_factor.description:
ACHIEVED realtime factor: sim seconds delivered per wall second,
measured, never the requested window over an assumed wall. 0 when
unmeasured.

requested_part.description: The part the board asked for (threaded through `McuBinding`, Track B).

short_pulses.description:
Firmware GPIO pulses that rose and fell inside one solver chunk on a
net clocking a TICK-evaluated sequential part (friction 1.16): those
parts sample once per chunk against the previous solve, so the pulse
was NEVER observed by them and their state in this run lags or misses
events, while chain-responder parts on the same board saw every edge
exactly. One entry per offending net. Empty (and omitted) on a run with
no such pulses.

spi_framing.description:
Per-SPI-bus transaction-framing tier: "exact" (framed on real CS GPIO
edges), "backend" (the emulator frames CS itself), or "heuristic" (the
chunk-boundary fallback, honest about its two documented failure
modes). Empty (and omitted) when the board has no SPI buses; mirrors
the web co-sim section so the CLI JSON carries the same coverage.

substituted.description: True when the requested part != the modelled core.

total_toggles.description: Total net toggles seen during the run. `0` => stalled/quiet.

unexercised_buses.description:
Bus peripherals (I2C/SPI slave models) bound on a platform whose MCU
backend models no matching bus controller (U3 finding 2): the firmware
never exercised them, so their state is the power-on default. Empty
(and omitted) when every bound bus device sits on a modeled controller.

wall_s.description:
Wall-clock seconds the headless co-sim loop consumed. 0 when the
producing path did not measure (older producers; the web mirror).

watchdog_limitations.description:
Per-MCU statements of how this backend's watchdog fidelity falls short of
the part. Non-empty means an armed, never-fed watchdog does NOT reboot
the core here the way silicon does, so firmware that HANGS runs forever
in simulation and every assertion about behaviour after a hang is
fiction: the run reads healthy while proving nothing about the recovery
path. Empty (and omitted) on a backend whose watchdog behaves.

watchdog_resets.description:
Per-MCU counts of reboots an unserviced watchdog actually performed
during this run. Not an error, a FINDING: an assertion that passed across
a reboot was measuring a rebooted core, not the run it claimed. Empty
(and omitted) when nothing rebooted.

chunk_s.description: The solver chunk it fell inside (seconds).

parts.description: Tick-evaluated sequential parts clocked by the net.

pulse_s.description: Narrowest completed pulse observed on the net (seconds).

limitation.description:
The backend's whole sentence, for verbatim display. Prose for a human:
do not parse it or match on it exactly.

resets.description: Reboots observed during the run. Always >= 1: a zero is omitted.

CrossCheck.description:
A cross-check the reader ran between two sources inside (or across)
artifacts, and whether they agreed. A disagreement additionally raises a
parser-limitation assumption; an agreement is positive evidence and belongs
in the inventory in its own right.

DrcGroup.description:
A group of clearance findings that share (net_a, net_b, layer, root cause),
collapsed to one line with a count. `at_limit` separates `gap == rule` (no
margin, but not below) from genuine sub-clearance violations.

at_limit.description:
True when every member sits exactly at the rule (gap == rule, no margin),
false when at least one is genuinely *below* the rule.

below_count.description:
How many of `count` are genuinely below the rule (gap < rule). The rest
are exactly at the rule (no margin, not below).

min_gap_loc_mm.description:
Board location (mm) of the tightest gap, so a UI can pan to the worst
spot of the group.

min_gap_mm.description: The tightest gap in the group (mm).

plain.description:
Human one-line description (`self.label()`), serialized so `--json`
consumers get the same text the human/`--plain` renderers show.

rule_mm.description: The clearance rule for this pair (mm).

DrcShort.description: A real short between two nets (gap <= 0: touching copper).

plain.description:
Human one-line description, mirroring `JsonFinding.plain` so every
`--json` finding category reads uniformly (SI/lint already carry it).

severity.description: Always "serious" for a short; carried for the uniform finding shape.

DrcStructured.description:
The DRC report, restructured into honest buckets: real shorts kept verbatim,
clearance findings grouped, and `gap == rule` separated from `gap < rule`.

at_limit.description: Grouped findings that sit exactly AT the rule (no margin, not below).

version_warning.description:
Set when the board's format is newer than hauksbee's validated copper
extraction (KiCad 10+), making the shorts above unreliable. Surfaced by
every renderer; CI gates ignore the shorts when it is set.

violations.description: Grouped clearance violations that are genuinely BELOW the rule.

EntityKind.description:
What results the assumption taints. Scope is the input to the on-path
decision: the causal-path traversal compares an assertion's subject nets and
refs against these, and only assumptions that match land in an
[`EvidenceMap`].

oneOf.description: A placed component or footprint.
One pin on a placed component.
A logical bus or peripheral.
An input artifact.
A board-level object that is not one of the narrower kinds.

ErrorBudget.description: How good a number is: integration tolerances, which method produced which time window, the accepted residual, the windows with no valid solution, and model uncertainty.

event_time_error_s.description:
Worst-case timestamp error for events, seconds. Today this is the
co-sim chunk quantization: an edge is observed at a chunk boundary.
Constructed only from a finite, non-negative value.

failed_windows.description:
Windows with NO valid solution: the run held stale values there. Any
quantity read inside one of these is not a measurement.

methods.description: Which method produced which span. One entry for a homogeneous run.

model_uncertainty.description: Interval bounds models place on parameters behind these numbers.

residual.description:
The accepted Newton residual, when the producing path measured one.
Present only when the producer measured a finite, non-negative residual.

tolerance.description: The solver settings the numbers were produced under.

EvidenceMap.description: What one assertion rests on: the artifacts, models, parameters and assumptions on its causal path, its error budget, and the status derived from them.

artifacts.description:
Indices into the run's `inventory`, causal only: the artifacts whose
contributions this assertion actually consumed. Omitted when empty, per
the module's serde convention: a check that reads no artifact says so by
carrying no key, and adding this skip after the schema publishes would be
the breaking change the once-only version bump is being saved for.

assertion.description: The assertion or finding this map belongs to.

assumptions.description: On-path assumptions, by id into the run's assumption registry.

coverage.description:
Statistical coverage wording for ensemble assertions. Not an
assumption: an accurate statement of method.

error_budget.description: How good the numbers behind this assertion are.

models.description: Models bound on the causal path.

parameters.description: Parameters read on the causal path.

status.description:
How much this conclusion is entitled to claim, derived from the
assumptions on its causal path.

EvidenceStatus.description:
How much a conclusion is entitled to claim, derived from the assumptions on
its causal path. Ordered by severity: `Clean < Qualified < Undermined`.

Use [`EvidenceStatus::as_str`] on every surface. One of the surfaces this
feeds is hand-serialized JSON rather than serde output, and a module whose
purpose is that surfaces cannot drift should not have five call sites
spelling `"undermined"` themselves.

oneOf.description: No on-path assumptions. The conclusion stands on evidence alone.

On-path assumptions exist but none is critical: the conclusion holds
with named caveats.

A critical assumption sits on the causal path. The conclusion is not
entitled to a verdict: invalid for analysis, exit-code-3 semantics.

IgnoredInput.description: One member or section of an artifact that was deliberately not used.

what.description:
The member: a file inside an archive, a section of a document, or a
sibling file the reader saw and skipped.

IntegrationMethod.description: The integration algorithm used for a solved window.

oneOf.description: Trapezoidal integration.
Second-order Gear integration.
Backward Euler integration.
Backward Euler after reducing the step.
Backward Euler after rebuilding the local state.
Backward Euler over recursively subdivided chunks.

IntegrationTolerance.description: The solver's convergence and truncation-error settings for this result.

chgtol.description: Charge tolerance, coulombs (capacitor local truncation error).

reltol.description:
Relative tolerance for Newton convergence and local-truncation-error
control.

JsonFinding.description:
One finding in the uniform machine-readable shape (§4.1): every check's
findings serialize the same way, so a CI pipeline or AI never parses prose.

actionable.description:
Whether a user should act on this (true for real findings and for
off-target info notes; false for within-tolerance observations).

fix.description:
A concise suggested fix, when a dedicated template applies. Closes the
TUI "no fix text" gap: once `JsonFinding` carries it, `Finding::from_json`
can read it instead of hard-coding `None`. Omitted (None) when no fix
template applies to this finding kind.

plain.description:
The same finding in plain language (best-effort; equals `message` when no
dedicated plain template applies).

JsonInputEvidence.description: Machine-readable input inventory for BOM/placement-aware runs.

JsonNote.description:
An info-level, never-`--strict`, always-emitted note. Distinct from
[`JsonFinding`]: a note never gates a CI pipeline and never changes an exit
code; it is the structured home for honesty annotations that must never be
silently absent (bind roles, co-sim substitution, coverage caveats, SI info).

oneOf.description:
A boot-sequence hazard about a specific MCU control net: driven HIGH and
held from reset, or left floating the whole run, with no bias resistor.
A distinct kind (not `Coverage`) so CI can filter boot hazards on their
own. Serializes as `"boot_control_net"`.

JsonWaived.description: One overruled finding on the machine surface.

kind.description: The specific rule it was matched on.

reason.description: Why the board's owner judged it wrong or acceptable.

subject.description: The finding's own message, so a reader can tell which one was overruled.

until.description: The date the waiver stops applying, after which this gates again.

MatchConfidence.description: Confidence in a model or parameter match.

ModelLayer.description: One layer of the model-resolution ladder.

oneOf.description: The producer recorded a resolved model but not which ladder layer won.

ModelOnPath.description: A model on the causal path.

layer.description:
Which layer of the model ladder it came from: "builtin", "pack",
"user-dir", "user-config-dir", "models-dir", "spice",
"engine-fallback".

reference.description: The part it is bound to.

ModelUncertainty.description:
Interval bounds a model places on a derived quantity. This is the socket for
interval models: shaped before its producer exists so that work lands in
this vocabulary instead of inventing a second one.

Both bounds are real numbers. A one-sided datasheet interval ("beta at least
100") has to be expressed with a finite other bound, because an infinity is
not JSON: it would serialize as `null` against a schema that says `number`
and no consumer could read it back. Whoever lands the producer picks the
physical limit and says so in `basis`.

basis.description: Where the interval came from ("datasheet min/max", "pack tolerance").

NetScope.description: The net and optional observation interval an assertion causally reads.

OverrideSource.description: How a user-authored override entered the run.

ParameterProvenance.description: Provenance for one bound parameter of one device.

parameter.description:
Reference-qualified, so an evidence map can select by part:
"R7.resistance", "U1.model", "Q2.beta".

ParameterRef.description: One model or input parameter on a specific causal subject.

Residual.description: The final accepted Newton residual, worst node.

at.description: The node or branch carrying it, for the "who" question.

max_abs.description: `max |f(x)|` over the residual vector at acceptance.

oneOf.description:
The whole run, e.g. every placed part treated as fitted because there
was no BOM at all.
Specific typed subjects.
One subject-qualified parameter.
Specific nets, optionally restricted to an observation window.
One named check ("drc", "si", "lint"), for `NotChecked` and `Waived`.

kind.description: The specific rule inside the check, when the scope is that narrow.

ThermalJson.description: Thermal in JSON: validity first, then the per-device peak temps when valid.

coverage.description:
Honest "N of M" coverage annotation, distinct from `validity`. Non-gating
by default (`partial:true` => the table is real but some power IC is open).

reason.description: Set only when `valid` is false: the named reason, listing offending refs.

TimeWindow.description: A sim-time window, seconds, half-open `[start_s, end_s)`.

UnresolvedActive.description:
One unresolved part that sits on a connected (active) net, with the
electrical consequence of defaulting it to open.

active_ic.description:
True when this part is an active IC (reference prefix U/IC/MCU): the kind
of part whose absence makes analog/AC/thermal results untrustworthy.

consequence.description: What leaving it open does to the analysis, in one plain line.

reason.description: Why it could not be bound (e.g. "no model; left open").

ValueOrigin.description: Where a bound parameter's value came from.

oneOf.description: Read from an input artifact, by index into the run inventory.

field.description: Which field of the artifact carried it.

oneOf.description:
From a resolved model. `layer` is the model source layer ("builtin",
"pack", "user-dir", "user-config-dir", "models-dir", "spice",
"engine-fallback"); `confidence` is the match confidence's display form
("exact" through "guessed").

layer.description: Which layer of the model ladder it came from.

oneOf.description: A documented default, naming the assumption that records it.
The user overrode it (an as-built overlay, a spec field, a CLI flag).

WindowMethod.description:
One window and the integration method that produced it. The primary method
covers most runs in a single entry; a per-chunk fallback ladder contributes
one entry per fallback-solved window, using that machinery's own stable
method names verbatim ("trapezoidal", "gear2", "backward-euler",
"reduced-step", "cold-start-backward-euler",
"subdivided-backward-euler").

accuracy_cost.description:
The accuracy cost, stated: empty for the primary method, a sentence for
a more dissipative rung.

description: The document `hauksbee run <board> --json` (and the per-report --json surfaces) emits. schema_version 2. GENERATED from `JsonReport` in crates/hauksbee-engine/src/result.rs plus the ok/verdict/serious_count/actionable_count rollup `to_json` prepends. Do not hand-edit; regenerate with: UPDATE_RUN_SCHEMA=1 cargo test -p hauksbee-engine --test run_report_schema_drift

assumptions.description: First-class assumptions collected from the real reader/bind path.

cosim.description: Machine-readable co-sim summary, present only on a co-sim run.

evidence.description: Per-net assertions derived from actual board incidence.

inputs.description:
Every explicitly supplied input and what it contributed to this run.
Empty on older/internal call paths that have no inventory context.

inventory.description: Exact inputs consumed by this run, content-addressed for reproducibility.

notes.description:
Info-level notes (bind roles, co-sim substitution, coverage caveats, SI
info) that must never be silently absent but never gate a CI pipeline.
Additive + `skip_serializing_if` so the schema stays backward-compatible.

schema_version.description:
Version of the `run --json` document contract. Bumped when a field
changes meaning or is removed; purely additive fields do not bump it.
The generated schema lives in `crates/hauksbee-engine/schemas/`.

waived.description:
Findings that fired and were overruled by an active waiver, with the
reason and the expiry date.

A green verdict that quietly dropped findings would be the worst of both
worlds, so the machine surface carries them exactly as the text report
prints them. A pipeline can watch this array grow.

title: hauksbee run --json report
